headline: Rough ski season dents profit; pass sales offer cushion
summary_short: Vail Resorts' fiscal Q3 revenue fell 7.0% y/y to $1,205M and net income dropped 19.3% to $314M as record-low snowfall and unusually warm weather cut skier visits 15.5%, though a 12.0% rise in effective ticket price and pass-product growth partly offset the decline.
summary_long: Record-low snowfall and unusually warm temperatures across the western U.S. cut skier visits 15.5% y/y to 7.28 million, hitting Mountain segment Reported EBITDA (-8.8% y/y to $579.6M) and Lodging Reported EBITDA (-44.6% y/y). Revenue fell 7.0% y/y to $1,205M and net income fell 19.3% to $314M. Effective ticket price rose 12.0% to $100.24 on guest mix, and North American pass revenue grew $25.1M, partly offsetting the visitation drop. Interest expense rose $9.4M on the 2030 senior notes issued last year. Cash fell to $371.4M (from $467.0M) and net debt rose to $2.7B (from $2.2B) after term-loan and note-funded borrowing. Management guided its core calendar-2026 capital plan at $215M-$220M ($234M-$239M including growth/RETP/real-estate capital).

drivers.explanation: Skier visits fell 15.5% y/y on record-low snowfall and unusually warm temperatures across the western U.S. that forced early resort closures, particularly at Rockies and Tahoe resorts; partly offset by a 12.0% rise in effective ticket price and $25.1M more North American pass revenue.

Mountain segment revenue and profitability fell on lower skier visitation from weather-driven early closures; cost savings from the resource efficiency transformation plan and lower labor/variable costs partly cushioned the decline.
Mirrors the Mountain and Lodging EBITDA declines from reduced visitation, partially offset by lower labor hours, resource-efficiency cost savings, and reduced variable expenses tied to lower revenue.
Same underlying drivers as operating income: weather-driven visitation decline outweighing cost discipline from the resource efficiency transformation plan.

Reflects the flow-through of lower Mountain and Lodging EBITDA from reduced skier visitation, plus $9.4M higher interest expense on the 2030 senior notes, partly offset by a lower effective tax rate (23.7% vs 24.0%).
Follows the Mountain and Lodging EBITDA declines from weather-hit visitation, partly offset by pass-revenue growth and lower labor/G&A costs from the resource efficiency transformation plan.
Tracks the net income decline; the diluted share count also fell y/y on continued buybacks, partially cushioning the per-share impact.
Same drivers as basic EPS: lower net income partly offset by a reduced diluted share count from buybacks over the trailing year.

Historic weather (record-low snowfall, unusually warm temperatures) drove a steep skier-visit decline, but the advance-commitment pass model and resource-efficiency cost discipline limited the damage; management left its calendar-2026 capital plan guidance in place.
